cautions: Lysine-poor; never balance a ration on corn alone.
name: Corn grain, ground

cautions: Must be heat-processed (toasted/roasted or commercial meal); raw soy carries trypsin inhibitors.
name: Soybean meal 44%

cautions: More protein than corn but lysine is still limiting; check stored grain for mold before grinding.
name: Wheat, whole/ground

cautions: Hull fiber dilutes energy fast; cap ~15–20% for broilers.
name: Oats, whole/ground

cautions: Color/vitamin A value, not an energy feed; cap ~5% in broiler rations.
name: Alfalfa meal, dehyd. 17%

cautions: Watch salt content and rancidity; >5% can taint eggs/meat flavor.
name: Fish meal 65%

cautions: Oyster shell dissolves slowly — preferred for layers so Ca releases overnight during shell formation.
name: Limestone, ground

cautions: Oyster shell dissolves slowly — preferred for layers so Ca releases overnight during shell formation. Offer free-choice as a supplement; formulated limestone carries the ration's base Ca.
name: Oyster shell

cautions: The reliable available-P fix — plant phosphorus is only about a third available (phytate), DCP phosphorus is fully available.
name: Dicalcium phosphate

cautions: Keep 0.25–0.5% of the ration: below it birds eat less, above it litter gets wet and toxicity is a real risk.
name: Salt (NaCl)

cautions: Ca and P vary by label (defaults here are 0 — edit them from your bag). Inclusion rate is the supplier's label rate (typically 0.5–1.0%); do not dilute by guessing.
name: Vitamin/mineral premix
